Question
========
ggplot2 offers both `facet_grid()` and `facet_wrap()` to split a plot into multiple panels. Which of the following statements about them are correct?

Answerlist
----------
* Both `facet_grid()` and `facet_wrap()` split the data into separate panels based on one or two categorical variables.
* Unlike `facet_wrap()`, `facet_grid()` lets you explicitly control which variable defines the rows and which defines the columns of the panel grid.
* `facet_wrap()` always arranges all panels in a single row, never wrapping onto multiple rows.
* If you facet by two categorical variables with n and m factor levels respectively, you need to display a total of n + m panels.


Solution
========
Both functions split the data into subsets and render one panel per subset. The real difference is control over layout: `facet_grid(rows ~ columns)` lets you explicitly assign one variable to the rows and another to the columns of the resulting grid, while `facet_wrap()` cannot align variables to rows in the same way and instead wraps the panels into a rectangular layout - which is exactly why it can span multiple rows rather than being restricted to one. Finally, faceting by two categorical variables with n and m factor levels produces n times m panels, one for every combination of levels, not n + m.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* True
* False
* False
